## Design patterns

<a id="AbstractFactory"></a>

### Abstract Factory

`AbstractFactory` · `src/patterns.ts:47` · status: **held**

A family of realizations chosen together, so that two families never mix: a database and the dialect its statements are written in.

Source: E. Gamma, R. Helm, R. Johnson, J. Vlissides, Design Patterns (1994), Abstract Factory

A choice that follows it has several ports chosen together.

| Followed by | Shape |
|---|---|
| [A SQLite file on the developer's machine](infra.md#LocalDatabase) | has the shape |
| [Postgres in production](infra.md#ProductionDatabase) | has the shape |
| [An in-memory SQLite database for the scenarios](infra.md#ScenarioDatabase) | has the shape |

- Maintained by: karim
- Followed by: [A SQLite file on the developer's machine](infra.md#LocalDatabase), [Postgres in production](infra.md#ProductionDatabase), [An in-memory SQLite database for the scenarios](infra.md#ScenarioDatabase)

<a id="Adapter"></a>

### Adapter

`Adapter` · `src/patterns.ts:12` · status: **held**

A technology made to answer an interface the service defines: the service depends on its port, the adapter on the technology (SQLite, Postgres, Node's HTTP server, the provider's API).

Source: A. Cockburn, Hexagonal architecture (ports and adapters), 2005 · `https://alistair.cockburn.us/hexagonal-architecture/`

A choice that follows it has realizations that touch the platform (implementations).

| Followed by | Shape |
|---|---|
| [Node's HTTP server](infra.md#HttpServerChoice) | has the shape |
| [The provider's API in production](infra.md#ProviderApi) | has the shape |
| [The system clock elsewhere](infra.md#RealClock) | has the shape |

- Maintained by: karim
- Followed by: [Node's HTTP server](infra.md#HttpServerChoice), [The provider's API in production](infra.md#ProviderApi), [The system clock elsewhere](infra.md#RealClock)

<a id="Repository"></a>

### Repository

`Repository` · `src/patterns.ts:35` · status: **held**

The reservations and the cancellations as collections: what answers them writes statements over a database port, and holds no driver.

Source: M. Fowler, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (2002), Repository · `https://martinfowler.com/eaaCatalog/repository.html`

A choice that follows it has realizations that are functions; realizations that reach another port.

| Followed by | Shape |
|---|---|
| [Reservations and cancellations as repositories over SQL](infra.md#SqlRepositories) | has the shape |

- Maintained by: karim
- Followed by: [Reservations and cancellations as repositories over SQL](infra.md#SqlRepositories)

<a id="Strategy"></a>

### Strategy

`Strategy` · `src/patterns.ts:24` · status: **held**

Interchangeable behaviours behind one interface, chosen without changing the code that uses it: a simulated provider and a stopped clock in place of the real ones.

Source: E. Gamma, R. Helm, R. Johnson, J. Vlissides, Design Patterns (1994), Strategy

A choice that follows it has realizations that are functions.

| Followed by | Shape |
|---|---|
| [A stopped clock in the scenarios](infra.md#ScenarioClock) | has the shape |
| [A simulated payment provider outside production](infra.md#SimulatedProvider) | has the shape |

- Maintained by: karim
- Followed by: [A stopped clock in the scenarios](infra.md#ScenarioClock), [A simulated payment provider outside production](infra.md#SimulatedProvider)
